case_name: Jane Antony vs V.M.Siyath on 25 September, 2008

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Jane Antony, wife of Antony, and her three minor children (Roshen Antony, Lisa Antony, Aleykutty Ittyavirah)
parties.respondent_defendant: V.M.Siyath, Vellooparambil, K.K.Mohammed Ibrahim, The Oriental Insurance Company Limited, Sophia Mary Antony, Sona Noru Antony

acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: The case concerns the right of succession of illegitimate children born to Christian parents. The appellants' claim is against the award passed by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal.

legal_principles.principle: The combined effect of Section 36 and Section 37 of the Indian Succession Act is that one-third of the estate of the deceased has to be first allocated to the widow, and the balance should be distributed among lineal descendants.
legal_principles.held: We are of the view that Section 36 and Section 37 of the Indian Succession Act should be read with Section 33 (a) and the combined effect is that one-third of the estate of the deceased have to be first allocated to the widow and the balance should be distributed among lineal descendants.

legal_principles.principle: Illegitimate children have a recognised status under the Indian Succession Act, and there is nothing in the Act barring them from succeeding to the estate of the deceased.
legal_principles.held: He also pointed out that there is nothing in the Indian Succession Act barring illegitimate children from succeeding to the estate of the deceased.

legal_principles.principle: The term 'children' in a Will or succession law includes only legal children, unless the testator intends to include illegitimate children.
legal_principles.held: In common law, the legal significance of the word 'children' if used in a Will is legal children and it will not include illegitimate children unless the testator intends to include them.

outcome.final_order: The court held that the right of succession of illegitimate children born to Christian parents needs a central legislation. The appellants are entitled to inherit the property of their father under the Indian Succession Act.
